TENDL-2023 evaluation was taken as reference as a result           925 1451   12
of analysis of neutron production (multiplicities, energy spectra  925 1451   13
and double differential cross sections) [1].                       925 1451   14
Residual product multiplicities in MF=6, MT=5 were replaced by     925 1451   15
PADF-2 evaluations [2] as follows. Since PADF-2 uses  MF=10, MT=5  925 1451   16
representation for residual product cross sections, their          925 1451   17
multiplicities were obtained by dividing by the total nonelastic   925 1451   18
reaction cross section MF=3, MT=5 from the reference evaluation,   925 1451   19
and written using the reference energy grid from MF=6, MT=5.       925 1451   20
Residual products from PADF-2 evaluation, which are not available  925 1451   21
in reference evaluation, were added to MF=6, MT=5 using LAW=0.     925 1451   22
There were few cases of residual products from reference file      925 1451   23
in ground and metastable state, for which PADF-2 evaluation        925 1451   24
considers only a single state, therefore reference multiplicities  925 1451   25
were not altered. Same concerns photon production, which is not    925 1451   26

************** G E N E R A L   I N F O R M A T I O N ************* 925 1451  218
                                                                   925 1451  219
This evaluated data file is based on a software system built       925 1451  220
around the nuclear model code TALYS [kon07], version 2.0. It is    925 1451  221
part of a large collection of isotopic evaluations, all created by 925 1451  222
running the system with either adjusted or default input           925 1451  223
parameters. This means that the data in the entire collection have 925 1451  224
been tested in detail for many isotopes against individual         925 1451  225
experimental data, while for other isotopes it is only as good as  925 1451  226
the global quality of TALYS at the moment. The mutual quality of   925 1451  227
all individual data files is however consistent: The same set of   925 1451  228
nuclear models is used and, equally important, the same ENDF-6     925 1451  229
formatting procedures for each isotope. The data file has been     925 1451  230
created automatically using the ENDF-6 format generator TEFAL.     925 1451  231
                                                                   925 1451  232
The resulting data file provides a complete representation of      925 1451  233
nuclear data needed for transport, activation, damage, heating,    925 1451  234
radioactivity, and shielding applications over the incident        925 1451  235
proton energy range from 0.25 to 200. MeV.                         925 1451  236
                                                                   925 1451  237
All transport and activation data for neutrons, charged particles, 925 1451  238
photons and residual nuclides are filed. This includes cross       925 1451  239
sections, angular distributions, double-differential spectra,      925 1451  240
isomeric production, discrete and continuum photon production      925 1451  241
cross sections, residual production cross sections and recoils.    925 1451  242
This general purpose evaluation can thus be used as both           925 1451  243
transport and activation library.                                  925 1451  244
                                                                   925 1451  245
**** N U C L I D E    S P E C I F I C   I N F O R M A T I O N **** 925 1451  246
                                                                   925 1451  247
None                                                               925 1451  248

***************************** T A L Y S ************************** 925 1451  250
                                                                   925 1451  251
TALYS is a computer code system for the prediction and analysis    925 1451  252
of nuclear reactions. TALYS simulates reactions that involve       925 1451  253
neutrons, gamma-rays, protons, deuterons, tritons, helions and     925 1451  254
alpha-particles, in the 1 keV - 200 MeV energy range. This is      925 1451  255
achieved by implementing a suite of nuclear reaction models into   925 1451  256
a single code system. This nuclear data file is based on a         925 1451  257
theoretical analysis that utilizes the optical model, compound     925 1451  258
nucleus statistical theory, fission, direct reactions and          925 1451  259
pre-equilibrium processes, in combination with databases and       925 1451  260
models for nuclear structure. The following output of TALYS is     925 1451  261
stored in this data file:                                          925 1451  262
                                                                   925 1451  263
- Elastic and non-elastic cross sections                           925 1451  264
- Elastic scattering angular distributions                         925 1451  265
- Recoil data                                                      925 1451  266
- Total particle cross sections, e.g. (p,xn), (p,xp),..            925 1451  267
- Total particle energy spectra                                    925 1451  268
- Total particle double-differential spectra                       925 1451  269
- Isomeric and ground state cross sections                         925 1451  270
- Residual production cross sections                               925 1451  271
                                                                   925 1451  272
For a description of the used nuclear models and their             925 1451  273
parameterization we refer to [kon19]. If for this specific         925 1451  274
nuclide we deviate from the global parameterization, it is made    925 1451  275
explicit above under Nuclide Specific Information.                 925 1451  276
                                                                   925 1451  277

##### MF3: REACTION CROSS SECTIONS                                 925 1451  286
                                                                   925 1451  287
All the data present in the following MT-sections have been        925 1451  288
calculated with TALYS, possibly normalized to experimental data.   925 1451  289
If the maximal cross section in an excitation function over the    925 1451  290
whole energy range does not exceed 1.e-9 b, the MT-number is not   925 1451  291
included. Cross sections lower than 1.e-20 b are assumed to have   925 1451  292
no physical meaning and are set to zero. All MT numbers extend up  925 1451  293
to the highest incident energy.                                    925 1451  294
The following reaction channels/MT numbers are generally included: 925 1451  295
                                                                   925 1451  296
- MT2      : Elastic scattering cross section: nuclear +           925 1451  297
             interference terms                                    925 1451  298
                                                                   925 1451  299
Obtained by integrating the "nuclear-plus-interference" angular    925 1451  300
distributions of MF=6.  Note that because of the interference      925 1451  301
effect, the tabulations in both MF=6 and MF=3 can be negative at   925 1451  302
some energies and angles.                                          925 1451  303
                                                                   925 1451  304
- MT5      : (p,anything) cross section                            925 1451  305
                                                                   925 1451  306
MT5 contains the reactions which can not be stored in any other    925 1451  307
MT-number. The information of MF3/MT5 can be combined with         925 1451  308
MF6/MT5 to obtain residual production cross sections particle      925 1451  309
production cross sections and (double-)differential cross          925 1451  310
sections.                                                          925 1451  311
                                                                   925 1451  312
##### MF6: PRODUCT ENERGY-ANGLE DISTRIBUTIONS                      925 1451  313
                                                                   925 1451  314
In MF6 we store all secondary energy, angle, and energy-angle      925 1451  315
distributions, as well as all residual and discrete + continuum    925 1451  316
photon production cross sections for channels other than capture   925 1451  317
(MT102) and reactions to discrete levels (MT51,etc.).              925 1451  318
All data are generated with TALYS.                                 925 1451  319
                                                                   925 1451  320
- MT5      : (p,anything) yields and energy-angle distributions    925 1451  321
                                                                   925 1451  322
MT5 contains, in this order,                                       925 1451  323
For neutrons up to alpha particles and photons:                    925 1451  324
- the production yields per particle for the whole energy range    925 1451  325
- the secondary energy-angle distributions per particles which are 925 1451  326
  not represented by explicit MT numbers. On a secondary energy    925 1451  327
  grid the relative emission spectra are given together with the   925 1451  328
  parameters for the Kalbach systematics for angular               925 1451  329
  distributions. Inelastic scattering cross sections for discrete  925 1451  330
  states have been broadened and added to the continuum spectra.   925 1451  331
For each residual product:                                         925 1451  332
- the production yields for the whole energy range.                925 1451  333
- the recoil                                                       925 1451  334
These distributions can be multiplied with MF3/MT5 to get          925 1451  335
the production cross sections and (double-)differential cross      925 1451  336
sections.                                                          925 1451  337
                                                                   925 1451  338
##### MF8: RADIOACTIVE DECAY DATA                                  925 1451  339
                                                                   925 1451  340
For reactions to isomers, MF8 designates where the information     925 1451  341
for isomeric versus ground state production, or residual           925 1451  342
production can be found, i.e. for each MT number it points to      925 1451  343
either MF6, MF9 or MF10.                                           925 1451  344
                                                                   925 1451  345
##### MF33: COVARIANCES OF NEUTRON CROSS SECTIONS                  925 1451  346
                                                                   925 1451  347
In MF33, we store the covariances of most, but not all, reaction   925 1451  348
channels that are given in MF3. All covariances are generated      925 1451  349
with the TASMAN code [kon19], which generates TALYS runs using     925 1451  350
a Monte Carlo parameter method.                                    925 1451  351
For each MT-number, the information consists of:                   925 1451  352
1. Covariances for MTa, Ea and MTa, Ea (variances)                 925 1451  353
2. Covariances for MTa, Ea and MTa, Eb (correlations for the       925 1451  354
   same reaction channel between different energies)               925 1451  355
3. Covariances for MTa, Ea and MTb, Ea (correlations between       925 1451  356
   different reaction channels for the same energy)                925 1451  357
4. Covariances for MTa, Ea and MTb, Eb (correlations between       925 1451  358
   different reaction channels for different energies)             925 1451  359
Classes 1 and 2 are covered by NI-type subsubsections with         925 1451  360
flag LB=5, followed by a LB=8 section which contains               925 1451  361
the cross section variances multiplied by 1.e-3. Next, classes 3   925 1451  362
and 4 are covered by flag LB=6 to account for the different        925 1451  363
energy grids that two correlating MT-sections may have. Since      925 1451  364
the total correlation matrix is fully symmetric, we only need to   925 1451  365
include the correlation elements between different MT-numbers      925 1451  366
once, and we do that in the subsection with the lowest of the      925 1451  367
two MT-numbers. We include covariance information for all the      925 1451  368
total cross sections, the lumped partial cross sections and the    925 1451  369
individual inelastic cross sections per level (MT51,...). We do    925 1451  370
not include covariances for MT600 and higher MT-numbers. For the   925 1451  371
most important channels, we include cross-channel correlations.    925 1451  372
                                                                   925 1451  373
